Ghanaian dancehall artiste Shatta Wale has announced plans to organise a nationwide campaign against hard drug abuse, calling on fellow musicians to join efforts to educate young people about the dangers of substance use.
The musician said he was considering bringing artistes from different parts of the country together for a public demonstration to raise awareness and encourage the youth to stay away from hard drugs.
Speaking in an interview on Afternoon Ride with Andy Dosty on Hitz FM , Shatta Wale argued that substance abuse could undermine an individual's ability to work, build wealth and make meaningful investments.
He cited his own business interests, including technology ventures, as evidence of the importance of remaining focused and productive.
“If I do hard drugs, I can't buy my cars, Lamborghini, Rolls-Royce, houses. I can't even invest in a lot of things,” he said.
The artiste disclosed that, beyond music, he was involved in technology, developing applications and digital platforms, which he said were progressing well.
He explained that he wanted to use the interview as an opportunity to amplify the campaign message and draw the attention of relevant authorities to the growing concerns surrounding hard drug abuse.
Shatta Wale said he was prepared to mobilise colleagues willing to support the initiative, with plans to extend the campaign to Takoradi, Kumasi and Tamale.
Among the artistes he mentioned were Stonebwoy, whom he hopes to involve from the Volta Region; Kofi Kinaata from Takoradi; Fancy Gadam from Tamale; and other musicians from the Ashanti Region.
He believes the involvement of popular musicians from different regions would give the campaign a wider national reach and help communicate the dangers of hard drugs to young people.
The proposed march, he said, would serve as a public awareness exercise, bringing entertainers together to support the fight against substance abuse.
